notes.x: A quadripolar (IS4) LV lead offers more pacing vectors than a bipolar lead. Medtronic quad CRT-Ds list 16 LV pacing polarities (12 bipolar + 4 extended bipolar), chosen for capture at the desired site, device longevity and avoiding phrenic nerve stimulation. Abbott IS4 CRT-Ds list ten programmable LV vectors. Phrenic stimulation can happen at higher LV output, and the labeling says to test for it.
src: “16 pacing polarities … avoids phrenic nerve stimulation … 12 bipolar vectors and 4 extended bipolar vectors”; “Phrenic nerve stimulation may occur as a result of left ventricular pacing at higher amplitudes … test for phrenic nerve stimulation”
“use an IS4-LLLL LV pacing lead and supports ten programmable LV pacing vector[s]”

notes.x: With DF-1, the high-voltage coils (RV, and SVC if used) and RV pace/sense plug into separate ports (DF-1 + IS-1). DF4-LLHH puts the high-voltage leads and the low-voltage RV lead on a single connector. Note: none of our saved sources gives a setscrew count, so we make no claim about it.
src: “Models without the “Q” suffix use DF-1 lead connectors for the high-voltage leads, and models with the “Q” suffix use a single DF4-LLHH lead connector for the high-voltage leads and for the low voltage RV lead.”
Figure 2 “Lead connections and setscrew locations, RA: IS-1, RV: DF4-LLHH, LV: IS4-LLLL”

notes.x: MultiPoint Pacing (Abbott) delivers more than one LV pacing pulse per cardiac cycle from the quadripolar lead. Biotronik labeling describes resynchronization through multisite ventricular pacing. In this app the “Multipoint LV pacing” feature row shows which models support it.
src: “MultiPoint™ Pacing delivers multiple LV pacing pulses per …”

notes.x: Biotronik DX ICDs use one ventricular lead but also sense the atrium. The labeling lists atrial sensing for type VR-T DX devices and says DX atrial sensitivity is intensified by a factor of 4.
src: “Sensing in the atrium: devices of type VR-T DX, DR, and HF”
“For the device type DX, the programmed atrial sensitivity is intensified by a factor of 4.”

notes.x: The -36/-40 suffix on Abbott models is the approximate maximum delivered shock energy listed in the labeling. Our dataset’s “Max energy” field matches it for every model checked (see decoder stats). Which energy is appropriate is a clinical judgment the labeling leaves to the physician.

MR-conditional labeling is specific to scanner field strength and to the complete implanted system (generator + leads). Some systems are labeled for 1.5 T only, others for 1.5 T and 3 T. BSC keeps separate component lists for 1.5 T and 3 T. Always check the full system against the manufacturer’s MRI manual.
src: “IMAGEREADY DEFIBRILLATION SYSTEM COMPONENTS FOR 1.5 T AND 3 T” (Appendix D)
